headline: Model Ridhika Ridhi found dead in Bashundhara
summary: The actress and model was found hanging from a ceiling fan on Saturday morning; police suspect suicide following a dispute during a video call.
details: Model and actress Ridhika Ridhi was found dead in the Bashundhara residential area of Dhaka on Saturday morning. She was discovered hanging from a ceiling fan around 6:00 AM and was later declared dead at Kurmitola General Hospital.
caption:

headline_marked: 7.7-magnitude quake in Indonesia: [[at least 38 people killed]]
headline: 7.7-magnitude quake in Indonesia: at least 38 people killed
summary: A powerful earthquake struck eastern Indonesia on Saturday, sparking mass evacuations and leaving dozens injured as rescue efforts continue under rubble.
details: A 7.7-magnitude earthquake struck eastern Indonesia on Saturday, killing at least 38 people, according to the National Disaster Mitigation Agency.
The quake's epicentre was located just off the north coast of the island, approximately 68 kilometres northwest of the coastal town of Ende.
Two people were reported trapped alive under rubble in the Manggarai regency, while approximately 2,000 people have evacuated their homes.
Residents in Nagekeo, the area closest to the epicentre, fled to higher ground after the sea retreated—a possible sign of a tsunami.
While the tsunami warning was later lifted, authorities warned residents not to return to damaged buildings due to the risk of aftershocks, with the strongest measuring 6.1.
Rescue efforts have been complicated by landslides that have cut off several roads, hindering access to the stricken areas.
Indonesia's location in the Pacific 'Ring of Fire' makes it prone to frequent and powerful seismic activity.
The region has a history of devastating quakes, including a 9.1-magnitude tremor in 2004 that killed over 220,000 people across the region.
caption:
A powerful 7.7-magnitude earthquake has hit eastern Indonesia, leaving at least 38 dead and thousands evacuated.

A 7.7-magnitude earthquake struck eastern Indonesia on Saturday, killing at least 38 people, according to the National Disaster Mitigation Agency.

The quake's epicentre was located just off the north coast of the island, approximately 68 kilometres northwest of the coastal town of Ende.

Two people were reported trapped alive under rubble in the Manggarai regency, while approximately 2,000 people have evacuated their homes.

Residents in Nagekeo, the area closest to the epicentre, fled to higher ground after the sea retreated—a possible sign of a tsunami.

While the tsunami warning was later lifted, authorities warned residents not to return to damaged buildings due to the risk of aftershocks, with the strongest measuring 6.1.

Rescue efforts have been complicated by landslides that have cut off several roads, hindering access to the stricken areas.

Indonesia's location in the Pacific 'Ring of Fire' makes it prone to frequent and powerful seismic activity.

The region has a history of devastating quakes, including a 9.1-magnitude tremor in 2004 that killed over 220,000 people across the region.
